newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen recouping some losses at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen recouping some losses at open.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 20507.85 +10.00 LME CASH NICKEL US$7135 -16.0
CANDLR 1.3923 LME CASH ALUM US$1571.5 -0.5
CAN 30-YR 116.06 +0.26 BRENT CRUDE US$17.84 +0.07
* Toronto stocks were expected to recoup some of their losses at the open on Thursday after a weak day Wednesday. * Analysts said trading would be volatile ahead of triple-witching Friday.

Toronto stocks were expected to enjoy a positive start on Thursday after falling more than 34 points on Wednesday, but analysts said trading would be volatile ahead of Friday's triple-witching session.

MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie said a positive bounce overnight by gold bullion and Canadian bonds, as well as a steadying of the Canadian dollar after losses yesterday bode well for today's session.
"So it looks like we're going to get a positive start to the day and I think we'll retrace a portion of yesterday's 34-point drop, but I don't think retrace all of it," she said.
Beattie said Friday's expiry of options, futures and options on futures -- known as triple-witching -- would add volatility to the market.
"Activity can be pretty weird on the Thursday and Friday of triple-witching, which is tomorrow, especially in the States," Beattie said.
"But the trend remains up, in both the U.S. and Canadian stock markets, which means the path of least resistance is to the upside," Beattie added.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 34.20 points on Wednesday to 6498.14 after the heavily weighted gold sector shed nearly two percent.

In economic news, Canada's merchandise trade surplus narrowed in April to C$1.72 billion from C$2.60 billion in March (revised from C$3.12 billion), Statistics Canada said on Thursday. The agency said overall imports hit a record high in April, as did imports and exports with the United States.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.9 billion in April, with exports of C$23.9 billion and imports of C$20.6 billion.
Canadian retail sales rose 1.1 percent in April to a seasonally adjusted C$19.12 billion from a revised C$18.91 billion (C$18.88 billion) in March, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.1 percent rise in retail sales in April after March's 0.8 percent drop.
